59407618.t: Prince Mohammed bin Abdul Aziz Park
59407618.s: Prince Mohammed bin Abdul Aziz Park is considered one of the most beautiful parks in Madinah because of its distinctive location: it lies on historic Mount Uhud and on the well-known ring road. The park offers a beautiful view thanks to its height on the mountain. On a visit to this special park you will see the beauty and splendour of Madinah, especially in the evening. The park also has plenty of green lawns and wonderful places to sit on the mountain, so it is a favourite destination for the people of Madinah.

59407618.a: Uthman ibn Affan Road, Jabal Uhud, Madinah

59407590.s: King Fahd Central Park is one of the six most beautiful parks in Madinah and is very close to the Prophet's Mosque, about five kilometres south of it. The park is known for its dense, tall trees, planted in an excellent layout, with seating among the lovely scenery and beautiful greenery, and it covers an area of 4.5 square kilometres.
59407590.b: King Fahd Central Park is one of the six most beautiful parks in Madinah and is very close to the Prophet's Mosque, about five kilometres south of it. The park is known for its dense, tall trees, planted in an excellent layout, with seating among the lovely scenery and beautiful greenery, and it covers an area of 4.5 square kilometres. The park is divided into several sections: one for families, one for the artificial lake and the mountains around it, and another for youth sports grounds, which has an area for horse and camel riding. There is also an area of farms and beautiful orchards with date palms stretching as far as the eye can see, and finally a section for children's games for all ages. Do not miss a visit to this beautiful park, which is full of attractions.

59407562.s: Al Awsiyah Historical Farm lies directly east of Quba Mosque in Madinah and has deep historical value, as its roots go back to the noble Companion Hilal ibn Umayyah Al Awsi (may Allah be pleased with him), one of the three who were left behind and whose repentance Allah accepted.
59407562.b:
Al Awsiyah Historical Farm lies directly east of Quba Mosque in Madinah and has deep historical value, as its roots go back to the noble Companion Hilal ibn Umayyah Al Awsi (may Allah be pleased with him), one of the three who were left behind and whose repentance Allah accepted.

The farm combines a traditional agricultural character with historical value, surrounded by tall date palms in the style for which the outskirts of Madinah were known in the past. It is only a few steps from Quba Mosque, which makes it a convenient stop for visitors to add to their visit to Quba Mosque and the Prophet's Mosque, especially when exploring the Awali neighbourhoods east of the city.
59407562.a: Tariq bin Abdulrahman Al Bajali, Al Khatim, Madinah

59407503.s: A tourist farm for the people of Madinah and its visitors, serving breakfast, lunch, dinner and coffee, where you can also buy dates, mint, roses and Madinah products.

59407485.s: The Jadat Quba market is visited by residents of Madinah and visitors from many countries. It stands out for its lively location among the old neighbourhoods and its varied products found in many corners. A pedestrian street runs through its centre, along with a group of hotels, residential towers and a number of sculptures. It is also known for an architectural style that echoes the local environment and the heritage of Madinah.

59407484.s: Al Fulk Al Bahri Park, restaurant and games are in Madinah and are a branch of the Al Qaswa business group. The idea behind Al Fulk Al Bahri was to provide a distinctive place offering a set of valuable, high-quality services worthy of the people of Madinah and its honoured visitors. The group aims for the Al Fulk Al Bahri park and restaurant to be the first choice for families and young people to spend the best of times.

59377804.s: Al Basta is one of the old neighbourhoods of Abha that still keeps the fragrance and simplicity of the past. It is a heritage district made up of a group of old buildings and archaeological forts, some dating back to the Ottoman era. On a visit you will find a public square and some old traditional shops. Al Basta lies on the banks of Wadi Abha in the city centre and is linked to the other bank of the city by an old Ottoman bridge built in the Ottoman period.

59329191.s: Ekrimah Dam is considered the first dam built in the Kingdom. It played a major positive role in protecting the city of Taif from the dangers of floods that constantly caused it damage, as well as in supporting the city's water sources.
59329191.b:
Ekrimah Dam is considered the first dam built in the Kingdom. It played a major positive role in protecting the city of Taif from the dangers of floods that constantly caused it damage, as well as in supporting the city's water sources.

The dam was built in 1375 AH (1955 CE) during the reign of King Saud bin Abdulaziz. A marble foundation plaque bears the date of construction, worded: "In the name of Allah, the Most Gracious, the Most Merciful. Ekrimah Dam in Taif. This dam was built in the reign of King Saud the First, King of the Kingdom of Saudi Arabia, may Allah support him with victory from Himself and keep him as a treasure for the Arabs and Muslims, in the year 1375 AH, Ministry of Agriculture." The writing uses several calligraphic styles, including Kufic, Persian and Thuluth.
59329191.a: Ekrimah Dam, Wadi Waj Road, Taif

59329189.s: Alkou Mosque, also called Al Mawqif Mosque, is one of the most important archaeological mosques in the city of Taif. It is called Al Mawqif (the Standing Place) because the Prophet (peace be upon him) stood at this spot when he came to Taif.

59329165.s: Al Madhoon Mosque is one of the archaeological mosques in the city of Taif. It is named after the mountain where it stands. It is also called Al Qantara Mosque, because it stands by the Ain aqueduct (qantara) that passed in front of it after it was built, and it is also called Qabil Mosque because it lies next to a farm belonging to the Al Qabil family.

59329163.s: Al-Kateb House is a historic house in the city of Taif, one of the cities of Saudi Arabia. It was founded in 1898 and is called "Qasr Al Niyabah" (the Deputy's Palace) because King Faisal bin Abdulaziz Al Saud stayed there during the summer. The King Abdulaziz Foundation chose it as the headquarters of the Centre for the History of Taif.

59329160.s: Al Dehlawi Palace is one of the most important heritage palaces in Taif and is also an architectural masterpiece, distinguished by a method of construction that reflects the Hijazi-Taifi culture of architecture. Several important figures have lived in the palace.

59329158.s: The historic Souq Al Balad is one of the oldest and largest markets in Taif Governorate and one of the most important historical landmarks of Taif.

59329112.s: Shubra Historic Palace, or Shubra Palace Museum, is one of the historic palaces in the city of Taif. It was built by Sharif Ali bin Abdullah bin Muhammad bin Abdulmuin bin Awn Pasha in 1323 AH (1904 CE) and completed two years later, in 1324 AH (1906 CE). It was turned into the regional museum of Taif Governorate and opened to visitors in 1415 AH, corresponding to 1995 CE. King Abdulaziz Al Saud and Faisal bin Abdulaziz Al Saud used it as a palace when they visited the city of Taif.

59329085.s: Abdullah ibn Abbas Mosque is one of the most famous mosques of the mountain city of Taif. It was built in 592 AH in the days of Al Nasir li-Din Allah Abu Al Abbas Ahmad ibn Al Mustadi of the Abbasid dynasty. It is named after the nearby cemetery of the "scholar of this nation" and its jurist, the noble Companion Abdullah ibn Abbas, whose death the Messenger of Allah had foretold and who was buried in Taif.

59329083.s: Al Samlaqi Dam lies at the head of Wadi Liyyah on the outskirts of Taif Governorate and is one of its historic dams. It is about 25 km south-east of the city of Taif. It is an old archaeological dam that was probably built before the rise of Islam, as early Kufic inscriptions appear on some of its rocks, and most of its sides still stand. The dam is notable for its size: it is 210 metres long and 10 metres wide, with a lower base 14 metres wide, and rises 11 metres above ground level.

King Abdulaziz Al Saud and Faisal bin Abdulaziz Al Saud used it as a palace when they visited the city of Taif.
59329080.b:
Shubra Historic Palace is one of the historic palaces in the city of Taif. It was built by Sharif Ali bin Abdullah bin Muhammad bin Abdulmuin Pasha in 1323 AH, then turned into the regional museum of Taif Governorate and opened to visitors in 1415 AH. King Abdulaziz Al Saud and Faisal bin Abdulaziz Al Saud used it as a palace when they visited the city of Taif.

The museum gives an overview of the palace's construction and the historical and political stages it has witnessed. It also holds a collection of stone tools, pottery pieces and panels of rock inscriptions and writings, as well as a section on crafts and industries in Taif, such as the extraction of Taif rose, and another section on the old market.

Inside the palace museum are archaeological remains, inscriptions and drawings on stone rocks, neatly arranged and hung on wooden shelves and stands. These remains were discovered in Taif Governorate and date back to earlier Islamic eras.

59329053.s: Saysad Dam is an old archaeological dam south-east of Taif in a naturally protected area. It was built in the era of the Umayyad caliph Muawiyah ibn Abi Sufyan and is one of the most prominent historical landmarks of Taif. An inscription in Kufic script is carved on the face of one of its rocks: "This dam belongs to the servant of Allah Muawiyah, Commander of the Faithful. Abdullah ibn Sakhr built it, by the permission of Allah, in the year fifty-eight. O Allah, forgive the servant of Allah Muawiyah, Commander of the Faithful, strengthen him, support him and let the believers enjoy him. Written by Amr ibn Habbab."

59329004.s: Al Shareef Museum is one of the museums of the Makkah region in Taif Governorate, founded by Ali bin Khalaf Al Shareef. It is a national museum inside a large traditional building covering 5,000 square metres and holds a large collection of heritage pieces of every kind, function and material that represent the heritage of the Taif region. The museum contains a small market made up of a group of stalls or shops, with each shop devoted to a particular craft and fitted with the tools and equipment of that craft. It also has halls for each group of items, such as weapons, with swords, rifles, daggers and spears in a hall of their own.

59329003.s: Souq Okaz was one of the three great markets of pre-Islamic Arabia, along with Souq Majanna and Souq Dhu Al Majaz. Its beginnings go back to 501 CE. The Arabs came to it for 20 days from the start of Dhu Al Qadah to sell goods and recite poems, until the 20th of the month. They then moved on to Souq Majanna to spend the last ten days of Dhu Al Qadah, then to Souq Dhu Al Majaz to spend the first eight days of Dhu Al Hijjah, and then set out for Hajj. The first inhabitants of Souq Okaz were the tribes of Adwan and Hawazin.
59329003.b:
Souq Okaz was one of the three great markets of pre-Islamic Arabia, along with Souq Majanna and Souq Dhu Al Majaz. Its beginnings go back to 501 CE. The Arabs came to it for 20 days from the start of Dhu Al Qadah to sell goods and recite poems, until the 20th of the month. They then moved on to Souq Majanna to spend the last ten days of Dhu Al Qadah, then to Souq Dhu Al Majaz to spend the first eight days of Dhu Al Hijjah, and then set out for Hajj. The first inhabitants of Souq Okaz were the tribes of Adwan and Hawazin.

After a pause of 1,300 years, Saudi Arabia revived Souq Okaz in 1428 AH during the reign of King Abdullah bin Abdulaziz Al Saud, as a tourist landmark of the Kingdom on the same site as the historic market. It is visited by many tourists from around the world and is also a historical gathering place for artists, writers, poets and all those interested in the history of the ancient Arabs. The souq offers cultural value through seminars and poetry and literary evenings, and organises a number of literary competitions and events across the Arab world, covering classical and colloquial poetry, short stories, drawing, handicrafts and photography. It has also revived the Diwan of the Arabs, from the finest poetry and the Mu'allaqat, in imitation of the poets of the Mu'allaqat. The Ministry of Tourism supervises Souq Okaz, after the Makkah Emirate supervised it for ten years.

59328954.s: Taif is famous for growing the Taif rose, which is used to produce rose water, perfumes, rose oil and other products. At the Taif rose house factory you can buy these products and learn how they are made.

59328930.s: The mountain cable car runs between Al Hada and the Al Kar area, 4 km long and at an altitude of 2,000 metres above sea level.

59328928.s: Al Kar Tourist Village is known for its summer climate, as it lies at an altitude of 900 metres above sea level. The village includes the lower station of the Al Hada cable car project, as well as water parks and two artificial rivers.

59328882.s: Ash Shafa is a centre of Taif Governorate in the Makkah region in the west of Saudi Arabia. It is famous for its beautiful nature and is considered one of the most important summer resorts in the Kingdom, constantly visited by tourists from all countries, especially from the Arabian Gulf states, who come to spend the summer holiday. It is one of the most beautiful summer resorts in the Kingdom.

59328880.s: The Alhuda area has distinctive tourist features because it lies on the western edge of the Hejaz mountains and looks directly over the plains of the Tihama region at an altitude of more than 2,000 metres above sea level. It enjoys a mild climate and distinctive mountain scenery, which has drawn interest in developing tourism in the area with resorts, hotels, furnished apartments, amusement rides, and family and youth seating areas, leading to its growth and development as a tourist resort. The area has great natural beauty and pleasant air during the summer.
